name: Immaculate Conception Catholic Church
history: The congregation began around 1845 as a mission of Savannah's parish, with a first church by 1847, destroyed by Union forces in the Civil War. Its 1874 replacement burned with most of downtown Jacksonville in the Great Fire of 1901. The present church was designed in 1905 by M. H. Hubbard and dedicated on 8 December 1910. It became a basilica in 2013.
arch: Late Gothic Revival, considered one of the best in Florida: a cross plan, pointed arches, window tracery, buttresses and pinnacles, high spires and a tall vault.
features: The architect also designed Bethel Baptist Institutional Church.
Its solemn dedication in 1979 means it may only ever be used as a church.

look.d: Its towers rise over downtown Jacksonville.
A great traceried window, one of the finest Gothic fronts in Florida.

fun: It represents Jacksonville's oldest Catholic congregation.
journal: Burned by war, burned by fire, and built a third time in stone.

quiz.q: What does its 1979 solemn dedication mean?
a: It can only be used as a church
